page: Microsoft Azure D48lds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Dldsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. This instance is equipped with 48 vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system features 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It includes 2835 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not feature any GPU accelerators. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated mathematical and machine learning operations.

Benchmark data highlights strong performance across multiple compute and data-processing workloads. The single-threaded gzip compression reaches a top-tier throughput of 36.36 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression registers a strong 302.08 GB/sec. In database and key-value store operations, the server demonstrates high efficiency, achieving a strong PassMark database score of 22353.15 and handling 79.57 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. For lightweight artificial intelligence tasks, the processor's AMX instructions assist in delivering top-tier text generation speeds of 338.79 tokens per second for a small 135M parameter LLM.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D48lds_v7 optimizes resource density by pairing high-frequency compute cores with a leaner memory profile. This design reduces the overhead associated with unused RAM for workloads that are primarily CPU-bound. The inclusion of a substantial 2835 GB local disk further enhances value by eliminating the immediate need for external storage attachments for high-throughput local operations. This configuration is highly suited for compute-heavy applications, static web serving, high-performance database operations, and lightweight machine learning inference tasks where CPU execution speed is prioritized over massive memory footprints.
